questions.question:
On the control plane (`{{CONTROL_PLANE}}`) enable the admission plugins **ImagePolicyWebhook** and **NodeRestriction** of the kube-apiserver.

The directory `/etc/kubernetes/admission` already exists on the control plane: it holds `webhook.kubeconfig` and its CA `ca.pem`. The webhook backend (`https://127.0.0.1:8443/image_policy`) is running on the control plane.

1. Connect to the control plane with `ssh {{CONTROL_PLANE}}`. The AdmissionConfiguration of the ImagePolicyWebhook plugin is already in `/etc/kubernetes/admission/admission-config.yaml` (next to `webhook.kubeconfig` and `ca.pem`): read it (the plugin must deny the images when the backend cannot be reached).
2. Enable both plugins (in addition to the plugins that are already enabled), point the API server to this file and make the directory available inside the kube-apiserver Pod.
3. Make sure the API server is healthy again. Pods whose image is tagged `latest` (or has no tag) must now be rejected by the webhook; Pods with a pinned image must still be admitted (you can test with `kubectl run ... --dry-run=server -n webhook-lab`).

verification.description: kube-apiserver enables ImagePolicyWebhook and NodeRestriction and has an admission control configuration file
The admission configuration is fail-closed (defaultAllow false), its kubeconfig exists and the directory is mounted
Pods whose image is tagged latest (or has no tag) are denied by the webhook
Pods with pinned images are still admitted by the working webhook

questions.question:
Confine a Pod with AppArmor, seccomp and the Pod Security Standards.

The AppArmor profile `secure-profile` is prepared on the worker node `{{NODE01}}` in `/etc/apparmor.d/secure-profile`. The Pod manifest `/tmp/exam/mhagou-001-q2/secure-pod.yaml` (Pod `secure-nginx`, namespace `secured-area`, node `{{NODE01}}`) is incomplete.

1. Load the profile on `{{NODE01}}` with `apparmor_parser`.
2. Label the namespace `secured-area` to **enforce** the `restricted` Pod Security Standard.
3. Modify `secure-pod.yaml` so that the Pod uses the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile and your custom `localhost/secure-profile` AppArmor profile, **is admitted by the restricted standard** and runs on `{{NODE01}}`. Create the Pod.

verification.description: AppArmor profile secure-profile is loaded on {{NODE01}} in enforce mode
Namespace secured-area enforces the restricted Pod Security Standard
Pod secure-nginx runs on {{NODE01}} with the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile
The container is confined by secure-profile (enforce): the programs it starts (busybox, the shell tools) are denied

questions.question:
Three checks on the nodes of the cluster.

1. **Kube-bench.** The kubelet of the worker node `{{NODE02}}` does not meet the CIS benchmark. Run `kube-bench` on `{{NODE02}}` (`ssh {{NODE02}}`), find the failing check about the kubelet's anonymous authentication (`--anonymous-auth`) and fix the kubelet configuration so that it passes. The kubelet must keep running.
2. **Checksums.** `/tmp/exam/mhagou-001-q3/manifests` holds copies of three control plane manifests and `/tmp/exam/mhagou-001-q3/SHA512SUMS` the known-good SHA-512 hashes. One manifest was tampered with: write its file name to `/tmp/exam/mhagou-001-q3/modified.txt` and leave the files as they are.
3. **Malicious process.** On the worker node `{{NODE01}}` a container runs a process called `cryptominer`. Find it (`crictl` or `ps`), then stop and remove that container only: the other containers of the namespace `crypto-watch` must keep running.

verification.description: The kubelet of {{NODE02}} runs with anonymous authentication disabled (effective configuration)
kube-bench check 4.2.1 passes on {{NODE02}}
modified.txt names the manifest whose checksum differs
The cryptominer container is stopped and removed from {{NODE01}}; the other containers still run

questions.question:
In the namespace `team-azure` run the Pods `messenger` (label `role=messenger`), `db` (`role=database`), `cache` (`role=cache`) and `reporter` (`role=reporting`).

A CiliumNetworkPolicy `baseline-allow` already allows the traffic of the namespace: leave it as it is.

Create a **CiliumNetworkPolicy** named `p1` in `team-azure` that **denies the egress traffic** of the Pods labelled `role=messenger` to the Pods labelled `role=database`. Everything else must keep working: `messenger` must still reach `cache`, and the other Pods must still reach `db`.

verification.description: CiliumNetworkPolicy p1 exists in team-azure and selects the role=messenger Pods
messenger cannot reach db and still reaches cache
The deny is scoped to messenger: reporter still reaches db

questions.question:
The files `/tmp/exam/mhagou-001-q5/Dockerfile` and `/tmp/exam/mhagou-001-q5/deployment.yaml` are insecure (files only: nothing has to be built or deployed).

1. Rewrite the **Dockerfile**: use a specific, pinned base image tag (not `latest`), run as a non-root user, and use `COPY` instead of `ADD`. Keep the rest of the image (curl, the archive in `/opt/app/`, the `CMD`).
2. Rewrite the **deployment.yaml**: remove the privileged access and drop all Linux capabilities (`ALL`).

verification.description: The base image of the Dockerfile is pinned (not latest, not untagged)
The image runs as a non-root user
COPY is used for app.tar.gz instead of ADD and the CMD is kept
The Deployment is valid and its container is not privileged
Every container of the Deployment drops ALL capabilities

questions.question:
Encrypt the Secrets at rest.

1. Generate a base64 encoded key: `head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64`.
2. Connect to the control plane with `ssh {{CONTROL_PLANE}}`. The file `/etc/kubernetes/etcd-encryption.yaml` is already there with the structure of the EncryptionConfiguration: replace `<YOUR_BASE64_STRING_HERE>` with your key.
3. Configure the kube-apiserver to use this file (it must also be available inside the kube-apiserver Pod) and wait until the API server is healthy again.
4. Create a **new** Secret and check with `etcdctl` (inside the etcd Pod/container) that its raw value in etcd starts with `k8s:enc:aescbc:v1:`.

verification.description: The API server uses an EncryptionConfiguration with aescbc first (valid key) and identity as fallback
The API server was restarted with the configuration mounted and is ready
A new Secret is stored encrypted (k8s:enc:aescbc:v1) in etcd

questions.question:
Falco runs as a systemd service (`falco-modern-bpf`) on the worker node `{{NODE01}}`.

1. Create a custom rule in `/etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml` (on `{{NODE01}}`) that triggers a **WARNING** when **any process reads `/etc/shadow`**. The output message of your rule must **start with `SHADOW READ`**. (Falco evaluates every matching rule on this node, so your alert is logged next to the ones of the default rules.)
2. Reload the Falco service.
3. Exec into the Pod `report-agent` (namespace `shadow-watch`, it runs on `{{NODE01}}`), run `cat /etc/shadow` and verify that the alert appears (for example with `journalctl -u falco-modern-bpf`).

verification.description: falco_rules.local.yaml has a WARNING rule for /etc/shadow with an output starting with SHADOW READ and Falco accepts it
The Falco service of {{NODE01}} was restarted after the rule was written and runs
Falco logs a SHADOW READ WARNING when processes read /etc/shadow in a Pod
release-bot only reads Pods and their logs
release-bot can roll out Deployments (get, list, watch, update, patch) but cannot create or delete them
release-bot cannot read Secrets or ConfigMaps and cannot escalate through RBAC
release-bot is still bound to a Role without wildcards; audit-bot is untouched

questions.question:
A Pod called `redis-backend` runs in the namespace `prod-x12cs`. It is exposed by a Service of type ClusterIP and listens on TCP port 6379 (it also listens on port 8080).

Create a NetworkPolicy named `allow-redis-access` in `prod-x12cs` that locks down the access to this Pod to:

- any Pod in the same namespace with the label `backend=prod-x12cs`;
- all Pods in the namespace `prod-yx13cs`.

Traffic is only allowed on TCP port 6379. All other incoming connections must be blocked. Use the existing labels.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy allow-redis-access exists, selects redis-backend through its labels and restricts ingress
In prod-x12cs only the Pods labelled backend=prod-x12cs reach redis-backend
The namespace prod-yx13cs reaches redis-backend, other namespaces do not
Only TCP port 6379 is open to the allowed clients

questions.question:
In the namespace `vault-lab` the ServiceAccount `vault-sa` and the Pod `immutable-pod` are defined in `/tmp/exam/mhagou-001-q10/strict-pod.yaml` (and already created).

1. Modify the ServiceAccount `vault-sa` so that it does **not automount** the API token by default.
2. Modify the Pod `immutable-pod` (re-create it: a Pod cannot be edited in place) so that it runs with `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` and `runAsNonRoot: true`.
3. Mount the token of `vault-sa` into the Pod yourself with a **projected volume** in `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount` (the file `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`).
4. Create an `emptyDir` volume mounted at `/tmp` so that the container can still write temporary files despite the read-only root filesystem.

verification.description: ServiceAccount vault-sa does not automount its token
immutable-pod uses vault-sa and mounts the token through its own projected volume
The token file inside the Pod belongs to vault-sa and comes from the projected volume
The root filesystem is read-only and /tmp is a writable emptyDir
runAsNonRoot is set and the process runs with a non-zero UID
